newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London quiet despite G7.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London quiet despite G7.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London saw thin trading on Monday, little affected by Saturday's Group of Seven (G7) statement on currencies, with little activity ahead of Japan's market holiday on Tuesday, traders here said.
After the 225-share Nikkei average in Tokyo rose 1.76 percent, the Nikkei 50 index in London was up just 15.4 points or 1.10 percent at 1377.18 on Friday's London close by 1445 GMT.

"The G7 statement has basically been ignored," a market- maker at one leading Japanese brokerage said. "Fundamentally the dollar is in the right area. And it probably needs to go higher on the interest rate differential between Japan and the U.S."
The dealer said the dollar was likely to remain the key influence on shares in Tokyo when trading restarts on Wednesday.
"The Tokyo opening will be steady. Blue chip exporter stocks with high dollar exposure will continue to be bought. Domestic stocks will continue to suffer," he said.
